rounds.facts: A emails B offering 500 widgets at $2 each, 'firm for 10 days,' signed. On day 3, before B replies, A emails 'never mind, sold them.' B then emails 'I accept.' Both are merchants.
rounds.subject: Contracts

options.label: UCC Article 2 governs
options.why: Widgets are movable goods, so Article 2 applies.

options.label: Firm offer irrevocable without consideration
options.why: A signed merchant's written assurance to hold the offer is a firm offer under 2-205.

options.label: Attempted revocation before acceptance
options.why: A tried to revoke during the irrevocable firm-offer period.

options.label: Mailbox rule timing
options.why: Whether acceptance was effective on dispatch is squarely raised.

options.label: Statute of Frauds ($500+)
options.why: A sale of goods for $500 or more must be evidenced by a signed writing.

options.label: Promissory estoppel
options.why: No facts show detrimental reliance by B.

options.label: Parol evidence rule
options.why: There is no prior or contemporaneous agreement being contradicted.

options.label: Impracticability
options.why: No supervening event made performance impracticable.

rounds.facts: Homeowner orally promises a painter $3,000 to paint her house over the summer. The painter buys $400 of special paint, then the homeowner cancels before any work begins, saying nothing was in writing.
rounds.subject: Contracts

options.label: Statute of Frauds (one-year clause)
options.why: The job can be completed within one year, so the one-year clause does not apply.

options.label: Bilateral contract formed
options.why: Exchange of promises to paint and to pay creates a bilateral contract.

options.label: Promissory estoppel / reliance
options.why: The painter relied by buying special paint, supporting reliance recovery.

options.label: Anticipatory repudiation
options.why: Cancelling before performance is due is a repudiation.

options.label: Consideration
options.why: The promised payment and promised work are bargained-for consideration.

options.label: UCC Article 2 governs
options.why: This is predominantly a service contract, so common law governs.

options.label: Accord and satisfaction
options.why: There is no new agreement to discharge an existing disputed debt.
